The divergence is real: bot_runtime.py:258-266 matches four bare substrings ('recorded for quality', 'call is recorded', 'whatsapp is recorded', 'recorded for compliance') and drives the dialog line at :280-283, while the canonical mentions_recording_disclosure (guardrails.py:30-56) requires subject call/conversation/chat or the 'recorded for <quality|training|compliance|verification|monitoring>' clause. Genuine divergences exist in both directions ('we are recording this conversation' → canonical yes, markers no; 'this WhatsApp is recorded' → markers yes, canonical no). But the auditor's own trigger example is WRONG: 'This WhatsApp chat is recorded for quality' matches BOTH — the marker 'recorded for quality' and the canonical alternative r'\brecorded\s+for\s+(?:quality|…)' — so the stated demonstration does not demonstrate anything. More importantly the consequence the finding leans on is conditional on GUARDRAILS-1 being fixed: today bot_runtime never passes recording_disclosed, so the two predicates never judge the same fact, and the sole live effect of a marker miss is one optional 'do not repeat it' prompt line on a channel whose prompt already forbids the disclosure outright (prompt.py:117-125). Latent, cosmetic today: TRIVIAL.
